steps: Electronegativity is how hard an atom pulls shared electrons. Use Pauling values.
ΔEN is the absolute difference of the two values.
Under 0.4 is nonpolar covalent. From 0.4 through 1.8 is polar covalent. Above 1.8 is ionic.

worked_example.q: Classify C-H. Carbon is 2.55 and hydrogen is 2.20.
steps: 0.35 is under 0.4, so the bond is nonpolar.

similar_problem.q: Classify O-H. Oxygen is 3.44 and hydrogen is 2.20.

problems.q: Classify the C-H bond. Electronegativities are 2.55 and 2.2.
problems.why: ΔEN = 0.35, so the bond is nonpolar.
hints: Subtract the two values. Do not add them.

problems.q: Classify the O-H bond. Electronegativities are 3.44 and 2.2.
problems.why: ΔEN = 1.24, so the bond is polar.
hints: Subtract the two values. Do not add them.
